issues.legal_issue: A mere order allotting surplus land does not complete its utilization for tenant resettlement when possession and required allotment formalities remain outstanding, so the surplus status may be reconsidered after inheritance.
material_facts: The landowner’s holding had been declared to include surplus land, and orders were made allotting that land to other tenants.
Before the disputed allotments were completed, the landowner died and two heirs inherited the land in equal shares, each with a holding below the permissible area.
The allottees had not taken possession of the disputed land when the heirs applied for reconsideration.
The authorities rejected the application on the ground that making the allotment orders had already amounted to utilization.
issues.conclusion: The allotment orders alone did not complete utilization. Because the utilization process remained incomplete when the heirs applied, the authorities could re-examine whether any surplus land remained after inheritance. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10-A(a) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, the State may utilize surplus land to resettle tenants. Section 10-A(b) saves land acquired by an heir by inheritance, so inheritance can affect utilization where an order has not been implemented. Rules 18, 20-A, 20-B and 20-C of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Rules, 1956 show that allotment is only an initial step: the allottee must obtain an allotment certificate, take possession, and complete the required documentation. Rule 20-D makes an allotment liable to cancellation if possession is not taken within the specified period. Thus, a mere allotment order does not complete utilization or pass completed title. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: surplus_land_utilization_dispute and heirs_inherit_land and allotment_order_made and allotment_process_incomplete_when_heirs_apply

predicates.surplus_land_utilization_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether land allotted to resettle tenants has been utilized as surplus land.
predicates.heirs_inherit_land: Heirs acquire the land by inheritance after the original holder's death.
predicates.allotment_order_made: An authority makes an order allotting the disputed land to resettled tenants.
predicates.allotment_process_incomplete_when_heirs_: When the heirs seek reconsideration, the allottees have not taken possession or the required allotment steps have otherwise not been completed.

issues.definition: When a surplus-land utilization dispute involves inherited land and the allotment process remains incomplete when the heirs apply, the allotment order alone does not complete utilization and the authorities may reconsider the land's surplus status.
